CP-1D.host_scope: identity, financial and bridge from the fixed H1 mapping (statements_only: identity and financial)
CP-1D.acceptance: exactly one ok read_inputs before the submit, and ok read_pages calls covering every page:N cited by the submit (evidence, accepted_basis, overall.evidence); the literal sequence is submissions.<case>.tool_calls
CP-1D.rules_mode: rules='journaled' with the core's RULES(text, seen) (docs/G1X-OWNER-CORE-PROTOCOL.md section 2, amended 2026-10-28), pure over the payload text and the session's Seen; it reuses live/tools.py unread_citation_issues (exact text 'Cited page not read through read_pages: <source_id> page:<n>', product sorted order) and UNBACKED_ABSENCE for any absence claim backed by a recorded search; G1-X calls it at submit and in the verifier in place of ToolRules().issues (which raises for a step that is not a tool-loop step). CP-1D's schema carries no ABSENCE_MARKERS value, so only the cited-page rule can fire; a missed read costs attempt 0 (S1a lease :131 pattern)
CP-1D.refusals: submissions.tool_refusals: cited_page_not_read (invalid attempt), invoke of any non-pack tool (refused receipt not_permitted recorded; no step journaled; no attempt consumed), submit before read_inputs (a raised WorkflowError not_permitted; nothing written)
CP-1D.view: read_inputs serves the exact context_block view, with no evidence lines: keys upstream [{module_id, status}], bridge {state, source_id, pages, items, totals}, cp1_facts, cp1_t417_rows, cp1_facts_note, inherited_limitations; quotable evidence comes only from read_pages

consumption.status: open until a consumer core reads the settled CP-1D head

consumption.edges: methodology.json lists CP-1D optional for CP-2, CP-2G, CP-2H, CP-3 and CP-4; CP-2G requires CP-2A and CP-2H requires CP-2G; CP-2G and CP-2H are unleased; cp2_synthesis reads CP-1 and CP-1A; cp3_relative_value.READ_OPTIONAL = CP-1A, CP-4; methods/cp4.md ruling 5; CP-6 has no edge; CP-5 counts only after a lease extends its integrity scope
consumption.closure: a lease amendment that has CP-2, CP-3 or CP-4 read CP-1D, or leases CP-2G/CP-2H, closes D3 (D3)

refusal_rules.order: Content issues follow shape issues; a shape failure returns alone. Issue text is frozen here; the validator must produce each expected_issues entry (prefix match where it ends in an open parenthesis) and no other.

basis_fraction_order.rule: The per-assessment basis/fraction rules are shape rules checked for each assessment in this fixed order; the first failure is returned alone for that item and the item's prose (rationale references) is not checked (LEAD ruling 2026-10-28)
steps: 1 accepted_basis or accepted_fraction given on another achievability: 'Accepted basis only applies to Partly supported: <label>' (basis checked first), else 'Accepted fraction only applies to Partly supported: <label>'
2 both given: 'Give either an accepted basis or an accepted fraction, not both: <label>'
3 neither given: 'Accepted basis or accepted fraction required for Partly supported: <label>'
4 fraction not a decimal above 0 and below 1 with at most two places: 'Accepted fraction must be a decimal above 0 and below 1 with at most two places: <label>'
5 basis quote not exactly one amount: 'Accepted basis quote must contain exactly one amount: <label>'
6 basis amount not above 0 and below the proposed amount: 'Accepted basis must be above 0 and below the proposed amount: <label>'

refusal_rules.recurrence: Saving requires Not applicable; Cost requires Non-recurring, Recurring or Not assessable; Not assessable only with Insufficient evidence (Cost, Not assessable, Insufficient evidence is valid: the gap legal-fees row)
refusal_rules.partly_supported: exactly one of accepted_basis or accepted_fraction; neither on another achievability; accepted_basis quote holds exactly one amount (a digit run with an optional decimal part) above 0 and below the proposed amount; Python computes the share as that amount over the proposed amount (one division, 38 digits half-even) and the accepted amount equals the cited amount; accepted_fraction is an analyst_judgment with two decimals in (0,1)
refusal_rules.confidence: High is refused whenever a bridge source is present (the evidence is management-supplied); with no bridge the rule does not apply
refusal_rules.no_bridge: no bridge source: any assessment is refused with 'Assessment given without a bridge in the pack: <label>' (no 'Unknown add-back' issues); overall.evidence must be non-empty ('the statements' add-back disclosure')
refusal_rules.r15_ruling: confirmed rule (LEAD 2026-10-28): when the pack has no bridge, overall.evidence (a located citation) is required so that tool use is never vacuous; any located citation satisfies it
refusal_rules.unparseable_bridge: a bridge source whose page:1 lacks the Basis line or the 'Item  Type  Status  Amount' header gives 'Bridge table not found' alone
refusal_rules.bare_figure: the core calls prose.issues(rationale, bound) and emits its text unchanged: exactly 'Bare figure: 1.2'; the module path for a settled claim prefixes 'Claim T1D.2.a02: '
